lineage_context.teaching_goal: Use Ginkgo biloba to teach the sole living ginkgo lineage: fan-shaped leaves with dichotomous venation, long and spur shoots, separate sexes, and naked ovules/seeds on stalks rather than seed cones.

project_scope.note: Ginkgo biloba is accepted and is the only living species of Ginkgoaceae. Kew treats its native range as southeastern China; project observations are cultivated/nonlocal comparison material.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: The leaf is nearly unique: fan-shaped blade, often bilobed, with veins repeatedly forking into two rather than forming a net.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Deciduous dioecious tree with long shoots and short knoblike spur shoots. Leaves may occur singly on long shoots or clustered on spurs.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: No flowers or fruits and no woody seed cone. Male trees produce catkinlike pollen cones on spur shoots; female trees bear usually 1–2 exposed ovules on a stalk.
family_diagnostics.seed: A mature seed has a fleshy yellow-orange outer coat and a hard inner coat; the fleshy coat is not a fruit.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Fan leaf + dichotomous venation + spur shoots + stalked naked seed = Ginkgoaceae.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: fan leaf → dichotomous venation → spur shoot → pollen cone vs ovule stalk → fleshy seed coat → conifer comparison
visual_lesson.intro: Ginkgo is useful because it breaks the idea that every gymnosperm is a conifer. It has broad leaves and no seed cone.

steps.title: 1 · Trace veins that fork in two
steps.look_for: Fan-shaped blade with veins repeatedly dividing dichotomously and no reticulate network.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the strongest whole-leaf family character.

steps.title: 2 · Find a spur shoot
steps.look_for: Knoblike short shoot covered with old bud-scale scars and often carrying a cluster of leaves.
steps.why_it_matters: Spur architecture helps connect leaf and reproductive structures.

steps.title: 3 · Separate male and female structures
steps.look_for: Male catkinlike pollen cones versus female stalk bearing usually two ovules.
steps.why_it_matters: Shows gymnosperm reproduction without a woody cone.

steps.title: 4 · Call the fleshy structure a seed, not a fruit
steps.look_for: Yellow-orange fleshy outer seed coat surrounding a hard inner seed coat.
steps.why_it_matters: Same mental-model correction as the juniper 'berry': gymnosperms do not make fruits.

steps.title: 5 · Joey Cupressaceae anchor
steps.look_for: Joey's Juniperus virginiana scale foliage versus Ginkgo's broad fan leaf.
steps.why_it_matters: Makes gymnosperm foliage diversity visually obvious using authoritative private-study material.

comparisons.title: Ginkgoaceae vs Pinaceae
comparisons.rule: Ginkgo has broad fan leaves and stalked naked ovules/seeds without a seed cone; Pinaceae has needle leaves and woody seed cones.

comparisons.title: Ginkgoaceae vs Cupressaceae
comparisons.rule: Ginkgo has deciduous fan leaves with dichotomous veins; Juniperus has evergreen scale/awl foliage and true seed cones with coalesced scales.

visual_lesson.caveat: Ginkgo biloba is a nonlocal cultivated comparison in this project; family recognition does not imply Central Texas nativity.

genera.fast_cue: fan-shaped dichotomously veined leaf + spur shoots + stalked naked seed

taxonomy_reconciliation.note: Accepted by current Kew; sole accepted living species of Ginkgo; native range listed as southeastern China.
